narrative.overview:
The site is laid out like a broadsheet edited by an engineer. Pages are built from rules, columns, and typographic hierarchy, not from boxes, cards, or imagery. A heavy 2px rule marks every structural boundary (header, page header, hero, footer), and 1px hairlines divide content inside those boundaries. Mono uppercase labels play the role of datelines and section slugs; large mono numerals act like column figures.

The palette is newsprint: near-black ink on white paper, three grades of grey ink, and a single Bauhaus Signal Red that marks the one or two things on a page that matter most. The density is editorial rather than app-like: generous vertical rhythm between sections, tight leading in headlines, comfortable leading in body copy, and line lengths held to reading measure.

Interaction is quiet until touched. At rest everything is ink and grey; a hover or focus answers with a single decisive response, either red text or a faint newsprint tint behind a row. There is no decoration that isn't also structure.
keyCharacteristics: Two-weight rule system: 2px press rules for structure, 1px hairlines for division.
Flat surfaces; depth comes from rules and tint, never shadows.
Geist for reading, JetBrains Mono for labels, figures, and metadata.
One accent, used sparingly; full light and dark themes via `data-theme`.

rules.name: The Two-Strikes Rule
rules.body: Bauhaus Signal Red appears at most twice per page at rest, the active nav item included. Hover and focus states don't count, because they are responses, not composition.

rules.name: The AA-Floor Rule
rules.body: Every text color passes 4.5:1 against both Paper and Newsprint Tint in its theme, including code tokens. Contrast is checked per theme, never assumed from the light one.

rules.name: The Ink-Grade Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy in text is carried by the three ink grades (ink, muted, faint) before size or weight. A new element picks its grade by importance: content, supporting copy, or metadata.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: Headings carry their own weight. No eyebrow or kicker label above a heading; metadata (date, tags, reading time) goes in a mono row below it.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Metadata Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for things a reader scans, never for sentences. If it's longer than about six words, it's set in Geist.

rules.name: The Negative-Tracking Rule
rules.body: Geist at title size and above is always tracked tight (-0.02em to -0.03em). Mono labels are always tracked open (0.04em to 0.12em).

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Box Rule
rules.body: Group content with a rule above it, not a container around it. If a new section needs a border on all four sides, it's the wrong pattern.

rules.name: The Flat-Press Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If an element needs to feel "above" another, give it a heavier rule, not a shadow.

rules.name: The One-Signature Rule
rules.body: The signature signing is the only authored motion moment on the site; everything else uses the shared fade-up entrance.

dos: Do separate structural regions with a 2px Press Rule and content items with a 1px Hairline.
Do set labels, dates, tags, and counts in JetBrains Mono uppercase at 0.6875rem with open tracking.
Do keep Bauhaus Signal Red to two uses per page at rest (Two-Strikes Rule).
Do respond to hover with either red text or a Newsprint Tint fill, at 0.1 to 0.15s.
Do define every new color as a token with a `night-*` counterpart so dark mode keeps working.
Do cap reading measure at 60 to 68ch.
donts: Don't round corners. Radius is globally 0 and must stay that way.
Don't add shadows, glows, or blur to express depth.
Don't introduce a second accent color.
Don't set sentences in mono or labels in Geist.
Don't wrap content sections in fully bordered boxes or filled cards at rest.
Don't use font sizes below the label token (0.6875rem) for readable text.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading.
Don't number rows or sections (01, 02...) unless the sequence is information.
